checks: Matched f9fd3b8e5ea799fa §§2 and 4, including actual endpoints, null point fibers and empty fibers. Each finite-tilt opposite cap has mass M−F because its boundary meets each interval at most at one point.
For positive and negative tilts respectively the cap tails are m₋+U₀ and m₊+U₀. The corresponding vertical cap masses include the entire own fiber and cannot lower the through-mark infimum.

For each side, convex interpolation with the actual mark proves nested slope intervals. Away from the finite endpoint set, the two indicator sequences are prefixes, so their nonzero differences have one sign. Taking absolute values before integrating therefore causes no cancellation error.

The transformation of each physical reflection pair gives the symmetric difference of the two slope intervals times k. The own loss is |2U₀−w₀|. With N≥2 there are at most 2(N−1) knots and 2(N−1)−1 changing intervals between them, each costing at most 2δ, plus an own loss at most 2δ. For N=1 only the own loss remains.
Replayed the exact interval reflection variation verifier, including the slope-prefix, depth and four-fiber reflection arithmetic.
